validity.researcher_notes: Existence: strongly confirmed -- FERC Docket No. CP13-492-000 (Pacific Connector Gas Pipeline, LP), later refiled as CP17-494 after the original certificate was denied in 2016 (154 FERC P 61,190, issued March 11, 2016) and approved in March 2020 (S&P Global Platts, 2020-03-19) before the developer withdrew all authorizations in December 2021 (OPB, 2021-12-01; EIA project_notes, Aug2026 release). Classification: correctly an interstate natural gas transmission pipeline (36-inch, certificated under NGA section 7(c) for open-access transportation service), not a gathering/lateral line -- confirmed by the FERC order and by EIA's own 'New Pipeline' project-type coding. Duplicate: checked against the full 42-row A7 roster -- no other row shares this route (Malin, OR -> Jordan Cove LNG Terminal, Coos Bay, OR); the nearest name collisions ('Northwest Gas Pipeline' P0230/P2626/P5101/P7790/P7812) are unrelated systems on different corridors (Sumas->Colorado, Madras->OR, Kalama->WA). No duplicate found. Route/endpoints, Length (229 mi) and Diameter (36 in) all confirmed within normal rounding across FERC (232 mi/36 in, 2013 filing), EIA (229-230 mi/36 in, all releases), and press (OPB, OregonLive: 229-230 mi). Two genuine concerns are raised separately below (Capacity spec; Owner% attribution) -- scope kept strictly to the PIPELINE per the dispatch's scope warning: the $10 billion figure quoted for the combined Jordan Cove LNG + pipeline project (OregonLive 2025) is NOT used for any pipeline-only cost cell.

validity.recommendation: Correct Capacity to ~1200 MMcf/d; sheet's 2024.00 MMcf/d matches no source found.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet Capacity = 2024.00 MMcf/d. No source found states this figure for the pipeline. Two independent origins converge on ~1200 MMcf/d for the certificated/refiled project (docket CP17-494, approved 2020, later withdrawn 2021): (1) EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook -- 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' = 1200 across the CP13-492 entity from the 2018-08 release onward AND the CP17-494 entity across all its releases (2021-01..2026-08) (one EIA origin per slice convention); (2) S&P Global Platts, 2020-03-19, independently states 'The 229-mile, 1.2 million Dt/d Pacific Connector pipeline would run through Klamath, Jackson, Douglas, and Coos counties in Oregon' (1.2 MMDt/d ~= 1200 MMcf/d). Note the ORIGINAL 2013 filing (docket CP13-492, denied 2016) proposed a smaller design capacity of 1.06 Bcf/d (1060 MMcf/d) per the FERC 2016 denial order -- this is a different, earlier filing vintage of the same physical pipe, not the value used here. Neither 1060 nor 1200 matches the sheet's 2024.00; this looks like a data-entry defect (2024 is not a multiple, sum, or obvious transform of any sourced figure -- possibly conflated with a year).

validity.recommendation: Verify Owner1% -- documented pipeline ownership was a 50/50 JV, not sole ownership.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet: Owner1 = Pembina Pipeline Corp, 100%. The only on-scope source found that both NAMES Pacific Connector specifically and ties it to Pembina is OregonLive, 2025-02-26 (via Wayback), which describes the pipeline as 'the controversial terminal and Pacific Connector Pipeline' abandoned in 2021, '...at the time backed by Calgary-based Pembina Pipeline Corp.' -- this supports Pembina as A / THE principal backer by 2021 but does not state a 100% share. The FERC 2016 order (also naming Pacific Connector directly) documents the ORIGINAL (2013) ownership structure: Pacific Connector Gas Pipeline, LLC (1% general partner, itself owned 50/50 by Williams Gas Pipeline Company LLC and Jordan Cove LNG L.P.) plus two limited partners each holding 49.5% -- Williams Gas Pipeline Company, LLC, and Jordan Cove LNG L.P. (wholly owned by Veresen Inc.) -- i.e., a 50/50 Williams/Veresen joint venture, not sole ownership. Pembina acquired Veresen in 2017 (Reuters, 2017-05-01, via Wayback -- confirms the $7.1B Pembina-Veresen deal and Veresen's Jordan Cove project, but this article and the Bloomberg 2017-09-22 refiling article both discuss only Jordan Cove/Veresen-Pembina, never naming 'Pacific Connector,' so neither is cited as a pipeline-specific ref per the relevance rule). No source found states Williams' original 49.5%+ interest was ever divested to Pembina/Veresen, nor that Pembina holds 100% of Pacific Connector specifically. Recommend keeping Owner1=Pembina Pipeline Corp (supported) but treating Owner1%=100% as unconfirmed pending a source that states the current full cap table.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Cancelled is still the correct status. Most recent independent evidence found: OregonLive, 2025-02-26 (via Wayback), reporting a startup (OA Partners LLC, per Mark Kekkonen) petitioning FERC to revive the abandoned Jordan Cove terminal and Pacific Connector Pipeline -- this CONFIRMS, rather than contradicts, that the project remains cancelled/dormant as of that date: the article explicitly states developers 'abandoned plans for the...Pacific Connector Pipeline in 2021' and frames the petition as an attempt to REVIVE a dead project (asserting federal preemption over Oregon's Clean Water Act certification, Coastal Zone Management Act consistency review, and Dept. of State Lands removal-fill permit, in the context of a 2025 Trump executive order on LNG). No FERC action, docket reactivation, or construction restart found as of this evidence date -- the revival is a petition/proposal only. EIA (Aug2026 release) still codes the CP17-494 project 'Cancelled' with no change since 2025-07. Confirming, not changing, Status. Noting the revival attempt in researcher_notes as relevant context for a future sweep, not as grounds for a status change.
